manasollasa.name: Manasollasa
manasollasa.summary: An early 12th-century Sanskrit encyclopedic text by the Kalyani Chalukya king Someshvara III, covering subjects from governance and astronomy to food, music and dance, and valued as a record of medieval Indian life.

kozhikode.name: Calicut
kozhikode.summary: Historic port city on India's Malabar Coast, capital of the Samoothiri (Zamorin) kingdom, visited in medieval times by Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta, Zheng He and Vasco da Gama.

malabar-coast.name: Malabar Coast
malabar-coast.summary: Southwestern coastal region of India stretching from Konkan to Kanyakumari, one of the subcontinent's wettest and most biodiverse areas.

dastarkh-n.name: Dastarkhan
dastarkh-n.summary: A traditional dining space used across Central and South Asia, originally a tablecloth spread on the ground or floor as a clean surface for food.

vijayanagara-empire.name: Vijayanagara Empire
vijayanagara-empire.summary: Founded in 1336 by brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, this Hindu empire ruled much of Southern India and was named after its capital city, now the ruined UNESCO site of Hampi.

muhammad-bin-tughluq.name: Muhammad bin Tughluq
muhammad-bin-tughluq.summary: Eighteenth Sultan of Delhi, reigning 1325 to 1351, skilled in several languages and interested in medicine, but nicknamed 'the Mad Sultan' for his erratic rule.

daulatabad-fort.name: Daulatabad
daulatabad-fort.summary: A fortified Indian city, originally called Devagiri, that was capital of the Yadavas, briefly the Delhi Sultanate's capital from 1327 to 1334, and later a secondary capital of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate.

bahmani-kingdom.name: Bahmani Kingdom
bahmani-kingdom.summary: A Persianate Muslim sultanate ruling the Deccan Plateau in India from 1347, often at war with the rival Vijayanagara Empire, before splitting into five states in the early 16th century.

kahwah.name: Kahwah
kahwah.summary: Traditional Kashmiri green tea preparation believed to have originated in the Kashmir Valley, widely drunk in Pakistan, Afghanistan and parts of Central Asia.

k-t-achaya.name: K. T. Achaya
k-t-achaya.summary: Oil chemist, food scientist, nutritionist and food historian (1923–2002), author of works including Indian Food: A Historical Companion.

chola-dynasty.name: Chola dynasty
chola-dynasty.summary: A Tamil dynasty from southern India that built an expansive maritime empire, reaching its height in the 9th to 13th centuries CE under rulers such as Rajaraja I.

shah-mir-dynasty.name: Shah Mir dynasty
shah-mir-dynasty.summary: A dynasty, named after its founder Shah Mir, that ruled the Kashmir Sultanate in the northern Indian subcontinent from 1339 to 1561.

sikandar-shah-miri.name: Sikandar Shah Miri
sikandar-shah-miri.summary: Seventh Sultan of Kashmir, ruling from 1389 to 1413, of the Shah Mir dynasty, nicknamed 'the Iconoclast' for destroying idols.

jamia-masjid-srinagar.name: Jamia Masjid, Srinagar
jamia-masjid-srinagar.summary: Friday mosque in Srinagar's Old City, commissioned by Sultan Sikandar in 1394 and completed in 1402, long a center of Kashmiri religious and political life.

narasingha-deva-i.name: Narasingha Deva I
narasingha-deva-i.summary: An Eastern Ganga monarch of Kalinga who reigned from 1238 to 1264, repelled Muslim invasions from Bengal, and built the Konark Sun Temple to commemorate his victories.

konark-sun-temple.name: Konark Sun Temple
konark-sun-temple.summary: A 13th-century Hindu sun temple in Odisha, India, built around 1250 CE, shaped like a giant stone chariot and once over 200 feet tall before its ruin.

eastern-ganga-dynasty.name: Eastern Ganga dynasty
eastern-ganga-dynasty.summary: A medieval dynasty that ruled the Kalinga region (mostly modern Odisha, India) from the 5th century into the 20th, remembered for building the Jagannath Temple of Puri and the Konark Sun Temple.

rajaraja-i.name: Rajaraja I
rajaraja-i.summary: Chola emperor who reigned from 985 to 1014, known for conquests across southern India and Sri Lanka and for commissioning the Rajarajeshwaram Temple at Thanjavur.

thanjavur.name: Thanjavur
thanjavur.summary: A city in Tamil Nadu, India, and former Chola capital, home to the UNESCO-listed Brihadisvara Temple built by Emperor Rajaraja I and known for its distinctive Tanjore painting style.

nataraja.name: Nataraja
nataraja.summary: A depiction of the Hindu god Shiva as cosmic dancer, one of the most recognized symbols of Hindu art, especially in bronze sculptures from the Chola period.

anantavarman-chodaganga.name: Anantavarman Chodaganga
anantavarman-chodaganga.summary: Eastern Ganga emperor who ruled from 1078 until his death in 1150, founding the dynasty, building the Jagannath Temple in Puri, and serving as a great patron of arts and architecture.

jagannath-temple-puri.name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
jagannath-temple-puri.summary: Hindu temple in Puri, Odisha dedicated to Jagannath, a form of Vishnu, famous for its annual Ratha Yatra chariot festival.

brihadisvara-temple-gangaikonda-cholapur.name: Brihadisvara Temple
brihadisvara-temple-gangaikonda-cholapur.summary: Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, completed in 1035 CE by Rajendra Chola I at his new capital Gangaikonda Cholapuram, among the largest Shiva temples in South India.

airavatesvara-temple.name: Airavatesvara Temple
airavatesvara-temple.summary: A 12th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva in Darasuram, Tamil Nadu, built by Chola emperor Rajaraja II and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

darasuram.name: Darasuram
darasuram.summary: A neighbourhood in Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu, known for the Airavateswara temple built by Rajaraja Chola II in the 12th century, a UNESCO World Heritage monument.

rukn-e-alam.name: Shah Rukn-e-Alam
rukn-e-alam.summary: Punjabi Sufi saint from Multan (1251–1335) of the Suhrawardiyya order, whose shrine there is one of Punjab's most historically significant sites.

tughlaq-dynasty.name: Tughlaq dynasty
tughlaq-dynasty.summary: Third dynasty to rule the Delhi Sultanate, from 1320 to 1413, reaching its greatest territorial extent under Muhammad bin Tughluq between 1330 and 1335.

golakot-jain-temple.name: Golakot
golakot-jain-temple.summary: Site of a medieval Jain temple complex in Madhya Pradesh, India, identified as an Adinatha temple whose sculptures resemble those at Deogarh.

arihant-jainism.name: Jina (Arihant)
arihant-jainism.summary: In Jainism, a soul that has conquered inner passions like anger and greed, also called an arihant or "victor," destined to attain liberation.

chaqchan-mosque.name: Chaqchan Mosque
chaqchan-mosque.summary: A Sufi mosque in Khaplu, Gilgit-Baltistan, dating from 1370, one of the oldest in the region and blending Tibetan, Mughal and Persian architectural styles.

khaplu.name: Khaplu
khaplu.summary: A city in Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan that was historically the second-largest kingdom in Baltistan under the Yabgo dynasty, guarding a trade route to Ladakh along the Shyok River.

amburiq-mosque.name: Amburiq Mosque
amburiq-mosque.summary: A 14th-century mosque in Shigar, Gilgit-Baltistan, one of the oldest in the region, with a stone core and carved wooden galleries.

shigar.name: Shigar
shigar.summary: A town in the Baltistan region of northern Pakistan, gateway to the Karakoram mountain range, inhabited mainly by the Balti people.

gilgit-baltistan.name: Gilgit-Baltistan
gilgit-baltistan.summary: Region of northern Kashmir administered by Pakistan, disputed with India and China; formerly the Northern Areas, it became a single administrative unit in 1972 and was renamed in 2009.

muhammad-of-ghor.name: Muhammad of Ghor
muhammad-of-ghor.summary: Ghurid ruler (c. 1144–1206) who extended his dynasty's rule eastward into South Asia, laying the foundation for centuries of Islamic rule there.

rajput.name: Rajput
rajput.summary: A large cluster of warrior-associated castes and clans from northern India whose kingdoms shaped much of central and northern India from the 7th century onward.

prithviraj-chauhan.name: Prithviraj Chauhan
prithviraj-chauhan.summary: A king of the Chauhan dynasty ruling from Ajmer who led a Rajput coalition to defeat the Ghurids at Tarain in 1191, but was captured and executed after their return in 1192.

ghurid-dynasty.name: Ghurid dynasty
ghurid-dynasty.summary: A Persianate dynasty from the Ghor region of central Afghanistan that converted to Sunni Islam and grew into an empire from 1175 to 1215, overrunning the Ghaznavids.

taraori.name: Taraori
taraori.summary: A town in Karnal district in the Indian state of Haryana, whose name derives from the word "Tarai."

mahmud-of-ghazni.name: Mahmud of Ghazni
mahmud-of-ghazni.summary: Sultan of the Ghaznavid Empire from 998 to 1030 whose campaigns extended his rule from Iran to the Punjab, laying the foundation for Muslim rule in the Indian subcontinent.

ghaznavid-empire.name: Ghaznavid Empire
ghaznavid-empire.summary: Persianate Muslim empire of Turkic origin that flourished from 977 to 1186, stretching at its height from the Oxus River to the Indus Valley.

chahamanas-of-shakambhari.name: Chahamanas of Shakambhari
chahamanas-of-shakambhari.summary: An Indian Rajput dynasty, also called the Chauhans, that ruled parts of Rajasthan from the 6th to 12th centuries, reaching its height under Vigraharaja IV before defeat by Muhammad of Ghor in 1192.

tomaras-of-delhi.name: Tomaras of Delhi
tomaras-of-delhi.summary: A Rajput dynasty that ruled parts of Delhi and Haryana in India from the 8th to 12th century, known mainly through inscriptions, coins and medieval legends, before being displaced by the Chahamanas.

jadaun-clan.name: Jadauns
jadaun-clan.summary: A Rajput clan of Indian origin claiming descent from Krishna's Yaduvanshi lineage, believed to have once ruled Mathura before shifting to Bayana and Karauli.

first-battle-of-tarain.name: First Battle of Tarain
first-battle-of-tarain.summary: Battle fought on 14 January 1191 in which the Rajput Confederacy under Prithviraj Chauhan defeated the Ghurid forces of Muhammad of Ghor, who escaped and later returned to win the Second Battle of Tarain.

ghazni.name: Ghazni
ghazni.summary: City in southeastern Afghanistan, historically the capital of the Ghaznavid Empire and today the capital of Ghazni Province.

firishta.name: Firishta
firishta.summary: Persian historian (1570 – between 1611 and 1623) who settled in India and served the Deccan Sultans as court historian.

second-battle-of-tarain.name: Second Battle of Tarain
second-battle-of-tarain.summary: An 1192 battle near Delhi in which Ghurid forces under Muhammad Ghuri decisively defeated the Rajput Confederacy of Prithviraj Chauhan, opening North India to Muslim rule.

khalji-dynasty.name: Khalji dynasty
khalji-dynasty.summary: The second ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate (1290–1320), founded by Jalal-ud-Din Khalji and best known for Alauddin Khalji's reign, when the sultanate reached its greatest extent.

ahmad-inaltigin.name: Ahmad Inaltigin
ahmad-inaltigin.summary: Turkic commander who served as treasurer under the early Ghaznavid sultans before becoming governor of Punjab in 1033, then rebelled and drowned fleeing a Ghaznavid army sent against him.

gangeyadeva.name: Gangeyadeva
gangeyadeva.summary: A ruler of the Kalachuri dynasty in central India who died in 1041; he began as a vassal but made himself a sovereign king in the 1030s and annexed Varanasi.

ibrahim-of-ghazna.name: Ibrahim of Ghazna
ibrahim-of-ghazna.summary: Sultan of the Ghaznavid empire from 1059 to 1099, whose long reign was considered a golden age for the empire due to treaties and cultural exchange with the Seljuk empire.

kannauj.name: Kannauj
kannauj.summary: An ancient city in Uttar Pradesh, India, once capital of several kingdoms and long fought over by rival empires for control of the Gangetic Plains.

madanapala-gahadavala-dynasty.name: Madanapala
madanapala-gahadavala-dynasty.summary: Indian king of the Gahadavala dynasty (r. c. 1104-1113) who ruled the Antarvedi country including Kanyakubja and Varanasi; his son Govindachandra, active in his administration, repulsed Ghaznavid and Pala invasions.

govindachandra-gahadavala-dynasty.name: Govindachandra
govindachandra-gahadavala-dynasty.summary: King of Kannauj from 1114 to 1155 and the most powerful ruler of the Gahadavala dynasty, who won military victories against the Ghaznavids and the Kalachuris.

bayana.name: Bayana
bayana.summary: A historical town in Rajasthan, India, known as the 'City of Bansasura', captured by Muhammad of Ghor in 1196 to guard Delhi's southern flank.

gwalior-fort.name: Gwalior Fort
gwalior-fort.summary: A hill fort in Gwalior dating to at least the 6th century, called the 'pearl amongst the fortresses of Hind' by Mughal emperor Babur and nicknamed the 'Gibraltar of India'.

pratihara-dynasty.name: Pratihara dynasty
pratihara-dynasty.summary: A medieval Indian dynasty ruling from Kannauj between the 8th and 10th centuries, which contained Arab armies advancing from the west and, under Mihira Bhoja, became one of the most powerful states in northern India.

chandradeva.name: Chandradeva
chandradeva.summary: Indian king of the Gahadavala dynasty who ruled the Antarvedi region, including Kanyakubja and Varanasi, from about 1089 to 1103 CE, and was the first sovereign monarch of his family.

vachana-sahitya.name: Vachana Sahitya
vachana-sahitya.summary: A form of rhythmic Kannada prose writing that flourished in the 12th century as part of the Lingayat Sharana movement, addressing social issues and personal devotion.

baba-farid.name: Baba Farid
baba-farid.summary: A 12th–13th century Punjabi Muslim mystic, poet and preacher (c. 1188–1266) revered by Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs alike.

guru-granth-sahib.name: Adi Granth
guru-granth-sahib.summary: The first compiled version of Sikhism's central scripture, completed in 1604 by the fifth guru, Guru Arjan, and later expanded to become the Guru Granth Sahib.

kambar-poet.name: Kamban
kambar-poet.summary: A medieval Tamil poet (1180–1250) who wrote the Ramavataram, a Tamil version of the Ramayana, along with several other Tamil literary works.

krittibas-ojha.name: Krittibas Ojha
krittibas-ojha.summary: Medieval Bengali poet (c. 1381 – c. 1461) who wrote the first Bengali version of the Ramayana, known as the Krittivasi Ramayan.

gona-budda-reddy.name: Gona Budda Reddy
gona-budda-reddy.summary: 13th-century poet and ruler in southern India who wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam, a Telugu retelling of the Ramayana.

ranganatha-ramayanamu.name: Ranganatha Ramayanamu
ranganatha-ramayanamu.summary: A Telugu-language rendition of Valmiki's Ramayana, written by the poet Ranganatha between 1220 and 1240 CE in about 17,290 couplets.

vidyakara.name: Vidyakara
vidyakara.summary: Buddhist monk and scholar (c. 1050–1130) who compiled the Subhashitaratnakosha, considered the most celebrated anthology of Sanskrit poetry.

shridharadasa.name: Shridharadasa
shridharadasa.summary: A Bengali poetry anthologist and feudal king remembered for compiling the Saduktikarnamrita, an anthology of Sanskrit verses completed in 1205 CE under the patronage of Sena emperor Lakshmana Sena.

madhava-kandali.name: Madhava Kandali
madhava-kandali.summary: 14th-century Assamese poet whose Saptakanda Ramayana is considered the earliest translation of the Ramayana into an Indo-Aryan language.

saptakanda-ramayana.name: Saptakanda Ramayana
saptakanda-ramayana.summary: A 14th-century Assamese retelling of the Ramayana by poet Madhava Kandali, among the earliest translations of the epic into a modern regional language and an early written Assamese text.

chandidas.name: Chandidas
chandidas.summary: A medieval Bengali poet (1339–1399), or possibly several poets sharing the name, who wrote over 1,250 poems on the love of Radha and Krishna.

birbhum-district.name: Birbhum
birbhum-district.summary: A district in the Indian state of West Bengal known as 'the land of red soil,' noted for its distinct cultural heritage and religious sites such as the Tarapith Temple.

maladhar-basu.name: Maladhar Basu
maladhar-basu.summary: 15th-century Bengali poet who wrote Sri Krishna Vijaya (composed 1473 to 1480), the earliest datable Bengali narrative poem, translating part of the Bhagavata Purana.

bhagavata-purana.name: Bhagavata Purana
bhagavata-purana.summary: One of Hinduism's eighteen major Puranas and a central text of Vaishnavism, promoting devotion to Krishna; it was the first Purana translated into a European language, in 1788.

mangal-k-vya.name: Mangal-Kāvya
mangal-k-vya.summary: A group of Bengali religious texts in verse, composed between the 13th and 18th centuries, narrating stories of rural Bengal's indigenous deities blended with Hindu mythology.

dattatreyayogashastra.name: Dattatreyayogashastra
dattatreyayogashastra.summary: A Sanskrit text likely written in the 13th century, the earliest known work to systematize hatha yoga under that name.

hatha-yoga-pradipika.name: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
hatha-yoga-pradipika.summary: A 15th-century Sanskrit manual on hatha yoga written by Svātmārāma, one of the three classic texts on the practice.

ruknuddin-barbak-shah.name: Ruknuddin Barbak Shah
ruknuddin-barbak-shah.summary: Ruler of the Bengal Sultanate from 1459 to 1474, the first to give prominent administrative roles to the Abyssinian community and credited as a pioneer of urbanisation in Bengal.

madhava-of-sangamagrama.name: Madhava of Sangamagrama
madhava-of-sangamagrama.summary: Indian mathematician and astronomer, c. 1340-1425, who founded the Kerala school of mathematics and was the first to use infinite series to approximate trigonometric functions.

kerala-school-of-astronomy-and-mathemati.name: Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics
kerala-school-of-astronomy-and-mathemati.summary: A school of mathematics and astronomy founded by Madhava of Sangamagrama in Kerala, India, active from the 14th to 16th centuries, known for discovering early power series for trigonometric functions before calculus was invented in Europe.
kerala-school-of-astronomy-and-mathemati.source_title: Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics

alauddin-khalji.name: Alauddin Khalji
alauddin-khalji.summary: Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate's Khalji dynasty from 1296 to 1316, known for major administrative reforms and repeatedly repelling Mongol invasions of India.

delhi-sultanate.name: Delhi Sultanate
delhi-sultanate.summary: A late medieval empire based in Delhi that ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent for over three centuries from 1206, through five dynasties ending with the Lodi in 1526.

hand-cannon.name: Hand cannon
hand-cannon.summary: The earliest true firearm, used in China from the 13th century and across Eurasia by the 14th, fired by manually lighting a touch hole.

shah-rukh.name: Shah Rukh
shah-rukh.summary: Son of Timur (Tamerlane) who ruled the eastern Timurid Empire from 1405 to 1447, controlling Silk Road trade and making Herat his capital and a centre of art and science.

abd-al-razzaq-samarqandi.name: Abd al-Razzaq Samarqandi
abd-al-razzaq-samarqandi.summary: A Persian Timurid chronicler, living from 1413 to 1482, who served as ambassador of ruler Shah Rukh and wrote a valuable account of his visit to Calicut in India.

timur.name: Timur (Tamerlane)
timur.summary: Turco-Mongol conqueror (1320s–1405) who founded the Timurid Empire across Central Asia and the Middle East, seen as one of history's greatest and most brutal military leaders.

malwa-sultanate.name: Malwa Sultanate
malwa-sultanate.summary: Late medieval kingdom in central India from 1401 to 1562, founded after the Delhi Sultanate's decline and eventually conquered by the Mughal Empire under Akbar.

gujarat-sultanate.name: Gujarat Sultanate
gujarat-sultanate.summary: A late medieval Indian kingdom based in Gujarat, established in 1394 and known to Portuguese traders as the Kingdom of Cambaya, until its annexation by the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1573.

srivijaya.name: Srivijaya
srivijaya.summary: A Buddhist thalassocratic empire based on Sumatra from the 7th to 11th century that dominated much of maritime Southeast Asia and its trade routes, especially with China.

harihara-i.name: Harihara I
harihara-i.summary: Founder of the Vijayanagara Empire in present-day Karnataka, India, ruling from 1336 until his death in 1355, and founder of the Sangama dynasty.

bukka-raya-i.name: Bukka Raya I
bukka-raya-i.summary: Emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire from the Sangama Dynasty, reigning from 1356 to 1377.

sangama-dynasty.name: Sangama dynasty
sangama-dynasty.summary: The founding dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire, established in the 14th century by brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I.

rajputana.name: Rajputana
rajputana.summary: A historical region roughly matching present-day Rajasthan, made up of numerous Rajput kingdoms with a strong warrior ethos, later administered by the British.

jaisalmer.name: Jaisalmer
jaisalmer.summary: City in Rajasthan, India, nicknamed 'The Golden City,' founded in 1156 as capital of the kingdom of Jaisalmer and known for its hilltop Jaisalmer Fort.

ranthambore-fort.name: Ranthambore Fort
ranthambore-fort.summary: A formidable hill fort in Rajasthan, India, founded in the mid-10th century, fought over by successive dynasties for its strategic, near-impregnable position.

chittor-fort.name: Chittor Fort
chittor-fort.summary: One of the largest forts in India, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Rajasthan that was the capital of the kingdom of Mewar, with dozens of palaces, temples and towers.

ghiyath-al-din-tughluq.name: Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq
ghiyath-al-din-tughluq.summary: Sultan of Delhi from 1320 to 1325 and founder of the Tughluq dynasty, who founded the city of Tughluqabad and died in 1325 when a pavilion collapsed.

sayyid-dynasty.name: Sayyid dynasty
sayyid-dynasty.summary: The fourth dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1414 to 1451; founded by Khizr Khan after he conquered Delhi, and later displaced by the Lodi dynasty.

vikrama-chola.name: Vikrama Chola
vikrama-chola.summary: Chola emperor from 1118 to 1135 who succeeded his father Kulothunga I and had earlier served as viceroy of Vengi, checking the ambitions of the Western Chalukya ruler there.

kulottunga-i.name: Kulottunga I
kulottunga-i.summary: Chola Emperor who reigned from 1070 to 1122 and also ruled as Eastern Chalukya monarch, whose accession began an era of internal peace and brought diplomatic ties with Cambodia, Srivijaya and China.

kulothunga-iii.name: Kulothunga III
kulothunga-iii.summary: Chola emperor (r. c. 1178–1218) who won wars against several regional rivals before a late defeat by the Pandyas began the Cholas' decline.

maravarman-sundara-pandyan-i.name: Maravarman Sundara Pandyan I
maravarman-sundara-pandyan-i.summary: A Pandyan king who ruled parts of southern India from 1216 to 1238, reviving Pandya power after centuries of domination by the Cholas.

hoysala-kingdom.name: Hoysala Empire
hoysala-kingdom.summary: A South Indian dynasty that ruled most of modern Karnataka and parts of Tamil Nadu and Telangana from the 11th to 14th centuries CE, known for elaborate temple architecture.

khums.name: Khums
khums.summary: An Islamic tax obligating Muslims to give one-fifth of acquired wealth, especially war spoils, first imposed in 624 CE after the Battle of Badr.

malik-kafur.name: Malik Kafur
malik-kafur.summary: General of Delhi Sultanate ruler Alauddin Khalji who led major campaigns across southern India, briefly seized power as regent, and was assassinated around 1316.

ibn-battuta.name: Ibn Battuta
ibn-battuta.summary: A Maghrebi Muslim traveller and scholar (1304–1368/69) from Tangier who journeyed about 117,000 km across Africa, Asia and the Iberian Peninsula and dictated an account of his travels, the Rihla.

sindh.name: Sindh
sindh.summary: A province of Pakistan along the Indus River, home to early South Asian settlement and later conquered by Arab forces in 712 CE.

gujarat.name: Gujarat
gujarat.summary: An Indian state on the western coast with the country's longest coastline, home to 23 Indus Valley Civilisation sites including the ancient port of Lothal.

rebellion-of-ismail-mukh.name: Ismail Mukh
rebellion-of-ismail-mukh.summary: An Afghan noble placed at the head of a 1346 to 1347 rebellion of Deccani amirs against the Delhi Sultanate, who abdicated in 1347 in favor of Zafar Khan, founder of the Bahmani Sultanate.

ala-ud-din-bahman-shah.name: Zafar Khan
ala-ud-din-bahman-shah.summary: Birth name of Ala-ud-Din Hasan Bahman Shah, founder and first Sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate from 1347 until his death in 1358.

taj-ud-din-firuz-shah.name: Firuz Shah Bahmani
taj-ud-din-firuz-shah.summary: Ruler of the Bahmani Sultanate in the Deccan Plateau of India from 1397 to 1422, who expanded the kingdom and fought repeatedly against the Vijayanagara Empire.

deva-raya-i.name: Deva Raya I
deva-raya-i.summary: Emperor of the Vijayanagara Empire from about 1370 to 1423, known for military campaigns, modernizing his army with imported horses and Turkic archers, and patronizing Kannada literature.

pagoda-coin.name: Pagoda (coin)
pagoda-coin.summary: A gold or half-gold coin, subdivided into 42 fanams, minted by South Indian dynasties like Vijayanagara as well as British, French and Dutch traders.

lingayats.name: Lingayats
lingayats.summary: A monotheistic Hindu Shaiva sect devoted to Shiva worship via a personal linga symbol, known for rejecting caste and Vedic scripture and for their devotional Vachana poetry.

basava.name: Basava
basava.summary: 12th-century Indian philosopher, poet and Shaivite social reformer traditionally regarded as founder of the Lingayat tradition; rejected caste discrimination and animal sacrifice.

shaivism.name: Shaivism
shaivism.summary: A branch of Hindu tradition worshipping Shiva as the supreme being, rooted in Vedic worship of Rudra, which became dominant in several Hindu kingdoms and later spread into Southeast Asia.

guru-nanak.name: Guru Nanak
guru-nanak.summary: An Indian spiritual teacher and poet (1469–1539) regarded as the founder of Sikhism and the first of its ten Gurus, who taught belief in one God and equality.

parashiva.name: Parashiva
parashiva.summary: The highest aspect of the god Shiva in Shaiva Siddhanta and Kashmir Shaivism, above the primordial Shiva and Sadashiva forms.

vidyaranya.name: Vidyaranya
vidyaranya.summary: Hindu philosopher and monastic leader of the Sringeri monastery from around 1374 to 1386, traditionally credited with helping found and guide the Vijayanagara Empire, though this is historically doubtful.

richard-m-eaton.name: Richard M. Eaton
richard-m-eaton.summary: American historian specializing in Indian history before 1800, known for work on Sufism, slavery and the Deccan and Bengal regions.

peter-jackson-historian.name: Peter Jackson
peter-jackson-historian.summary: British historian and emeritus professor at Keele University, specializing in the Crusades and contacts between Europeans, Mongols and medieval Muslim India.

vaishya.name: Vaishya
vaishya.summary: One of the four varnas of the traditional Hindu social order in India, associated with agriculture, cattle-keeping and trade.

shudra.name: Shudra
shudra.summary: One of the four varnas of the traditional Hindu class system in ancient India, roughly a laborer class, though its real social meaning varied and grew unclear by medieval times.

kshatriya.name: Kshatriya
kshatriya.summary: One of the four varnas, or social orders, of Hindu society, associated with the ruling and warrior aristocracy.

ram-sharan-sharma.name: Ram Sharan Sharma
ram-sharan-sharma.summary: Marxist historian and Indologist (1919–2011) specializing in Ancient and early Medieval India, who taught at Patna and Delhi University and founded the Indian Council of Historical Research.

chaturanga.name: Chaturanga
chaturanga.summary: An ancient Indian strategy board game known from around the 7th century CE, considered the common ancestor of chess and related games across Asia.

nalanda-mahavihara.name: Nalanda
nalanda-mahavihara.summary: A renowned Buddhist monastery and centre of learning in medieval Bihar, India, operating from about 427 to 1400 CE and often called the world's first residential university.

kalinga-region.name: Kalinga
kalinga-region.summary: A historical region of eastern coastal India between the Ganges and Godavari rivers, roughly matching modern Odisha, ruled by many regional dynasties over the centuries.

pala-empire.name: Pala Empire
pala-empire.summary: An early medieval Indian empire based in Bengal and Bihar from the late 8th century, noted for its war elephants and navy and for sponsoring Buddhist institutions.

khorasan.name: Khorasan
khorasan.summary: A historical region of the Iranian Plateau spanning parts of modern Afghanistan, Iran and Central Asia, with boundaries that varied over time and roots reaching back to Bronze Age complex societies there.

hoshang-shah-s-invasion-of-orissa.name: Bhanudeva IV
hoshang-shah-s-invasion-of-orissa.summary: King of Orissa's Eastern Ganga dynasty (r. 1414–1434) who was captured in 1422 by Sultan Hoshang Shah's disguised horsemen and held hostage until a ransom of 75 elephants was paid.

deccan-sultanates.name: Deccan sultanates
deccan-sultanates.summary: Five Persianate Muslim kingdoms that arose on the Deccan Plateau after the Bahmani Sultanate broke apart in the late 15th century; they later allied to defeat the Vijayanagara Empire in 1565.

jamal-ad-din-ii.name: Jamal ad-Din II
jamal-ad-din-ii.summary: A Sultan of the Adal Sultanate who died in 1433, the youngest son of Sa'ad ad-Din II.

ludovico-di-varthema.name: Ludovico di Varthema
ludovico-di-varthema.summary: Italian traveller and diarist (c. 1470–1517), one of the first non-Muslim Europeans known to have entered Mecca as a pilgrim.

zeila.name: Zeila
zeila.summary: A historic port town in what is now Somaliland, capital of the early Adal Kingdom by the 9th century and the Ifat Sultanate in the 13th, later under Ottoman and then British control.
